name: MarkItDown MCP
summary: Microsoft's local MCP server converts explicitly supplied file, HTTP, HTTPS, and data URIs to Markdown through one read-only tool.

prerequisites: Explicitly bounded file and network access for the server process
Third-party plugins disabled by leaving MARKITDOWN_ENABLE_PLUGINS unset or false

reads: Any local file readable by the server account when given a file URI
Any HTTP or HTTPS resource reachable from the server process, plus caller-supplied data URIs

details: The convert_to_markdown tool accepts file, HTTP, HTTPS, and data URIs, so every call must be treated as an explicit sensitive-read boundary
The server has no authentication and runs with the privileges and network reachability of its process
Keep HTTP or SSE bound to localhost and prefer a sandbox or container with narrow mounts when converting untrusted content
This reviewed profile excludes third-party plugins; keep MARKITDOWN_ENABLE_PLUGINS unset or false because enabled plugins widen the process execution boundary

confirmation.notes: Confirm installation and the exact URI before each conversion; reject broad local paths, private-network targets, or untrusted remote content unless their read boundary is explicitly approved.

host_evidence.surface: OpenClaw CLI mcp add/probe/doctor/show/list/unset commands and one headless agent exec turn using the claude-cli runtime, prompted to convert one local file (call arguments not retained); Gateway, channels, interactive sessions, and HTTP or HTTPS conversions were not tested.
host_evidence.credentials: None for MarkItDown; operator-observed, not captured: the model turn used the operator's existing Claude Code login. The credential-like tables listed in the state inspection had zero rows; Claude Code's own credential storage was not inspected.
egress: The prompt requested a file: URI conversion; call arguments were not retained.
The model turn reports anthropic as its provider; network traffic was not monitored, so no destination was measured.
host_evidence.side_effects: One reported read-only tool call; the reply matched the synthetic fixture. After uninstall the state directory held openclaw.json, openclaw.json.bak, SQLite databases, plugin skill files, and lock files; no destructive command appears in the retained procedure, and writes outside that directory were not monitored.
host_evidence.confirmation_gates: No confirmation event in the headless agent exec result; the operator must confirm the exact URI before each conversion.

health_check.output_shape: One tool, markitdown__convert_to_markdown; one per-server tool; empty diagnostics.

host_evidence.uninstall: openclaw mcp unset markitdown plus uv pip uninstall markitdown-mcp markitdown removed the managed entry and packages. Residue remained in openclaw.json.bak and state SQLite rows; no integration credential appears in the retained config, and revocation was not tested.

health_check: Run the stdio server in a sandbox, list its single convert_to_markdown tool, then convert one non-sensitive local fixture from an explicitly allowed directory.

uninstall.instructions: Remove the MarkItDown MCP entry from the client and uninstall markitdown-mcp or remove its container image; preserve every source file and converted output unless separately requested.
